title: Converting Units of Length, Mass and Capacity
seo_title: Grade 4 Converting Metric Units Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 4)
standard_text: Convert common units of measure from larger to smaller units, and vice versa: meter and centimeter, kilometer and meter, kilogram and gram, gram and milligram, and liter and milliliter.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 metric conversion worksheets for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: meters and centimeters, kilometers and meters, kilograms, grams and milligrams, liters and milliliters. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Bigger to smaller unit: multiply. Smaller to bigger: divide.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • 1 m = 100 cm, 1 km = 1,000 m, 1 kg = 1,000 g, 1 g = 1,000 mg, 1 L = 1,000 mL.
  • From a bigger unit to a smaller unit, multiply (you need more of the small units).
  • From a smaller unit to a bigger unit, divide.
  • Before you compare or add measurements, write them in the same unit.

Examples

Example

3 kg 250 g

3 kg = 3,000 g

3,000 + 250

Answer: 3,250 g

Example

4,500 mL

4,500 ÷ 1,000

Answer: 4 L 500 mL

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Multiplying to get a bigger unitcm to m: divide by 100.
Using 100 for every unitOnly m and cm use 100; the others use 1,000.
Comparing different unitsChange to the same unit first.

faq.q: What does MATATAG Math 4 ask about units?
faq.a: Convert common units of measure from larger to smaller units, and vice versa: meter and centimeter, kilometer and meter, kilogram and gram, gram and milligram, and liter and milliliter.
For very light things, like the amount of medicine in a tablet.

faq.q: How many centimeters are in a kilometer?

items.q: How many millimeters are in 1 centimeter?
items.e: Look at a ruler: there are 10 small marks in each centimeter. 1 cm = 10 mm.

items.q: How many centimeters are in 1 meter?
items.e: Centi means one hundredth, so 1 m = 100 cm. A meter stick has 100 cm marked on it.

items.q: How many meters are in 1 kilometer?
items.e: Kilo means 1,000, so 1 km = 1,000 m (not 100 m).

items.q: About how tall is a classroom door?
items.e: A door is a little taller than a grown-up, about 2 meters. 2 cm is shorter than your finger.

items.q: Pupils walk for about 15 minutes. About how far do they go?
items.e: In 15 minutes you can walk about 1 kilometer (1,000 m). 1 m is just one big step.

items.q: Convert. 6 cm = ☐ mm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm. Centimeters are bigger than millimeters, so you need more millimeters: multiply. 6 × 10 = 60, so 6 cm = 60 mm.

items.q: Convert. 7 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Meters are bigger than centimeters, so you need more centimeters: multiply. 7 × 100 = 700, so 7 m = 700 cm.

items.q: Convert. 4 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Kilometers are bigger than meters, so you need more meters: multiply. 4 × 1,000 = 4,000, so 4 km = 4,000 m.

items.q: Convert. 90 mm = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm. Centimeters are bigger than millimeters, so you need fewer centimeters: divide. 90 ÷ 10 = 9, so 90 mm = 9 cm.

items.q: Convert. 800 cm = ☐ m
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Meters are bigger than centimeters, so you need fewer meters: divide. 800 ÷ 100 = 8, so 800 cm = 8 m.

items.q: Convert. 9,000 m = ☐ km
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Kilometers are bigger than meters, so you need fewer kilometers: divide. 9,000 ÷ 1,000 = 9, so 9,000 m = 9 km.

items.q: Convert. 12 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Kilometers are bigger than meters, so you need more meters: multiply. 12 × 1,000 = 12,000, so 12 km = 12,000 m.
The pencil ends 4 small marks after 6 cm, so it is 6 cm 4 mm long. 1 cm = 10 mm, so 6 × 10 = 60, and 60 + 4 = 64 mm.
The pencil reaches 5 whole centimeters and then 7 small marks. Each small mark is 1 mm, so it is 5 cm 7 mm long (57 mm).
The pencil starts at 1 cm, not at 0. It ends at 8 cm 3 mm = 83 mm. Take away the start: 83 − 10 = 73 mm.

items.q: How many meters are in 12 km?
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Half of 1,000 is 500, so 12 km = 500 m. 50 m would mean 1 km = 100 m.

items.q: How many grams are in 14 kg?
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. To find a quarter, divide by 4: 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 g.

items.q: How many milliliters are in 34 l?
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. One quarter is 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 mL, so three quarters is 3 × 250 = 750 mL.

items.q: Convert. 1.5 L = ☐ mL
Convert. 2.5 km = ☐ m
items.e: 2 km = 2,000 m, and 0.5 km is half a kilometer = 500 m. 2,000 + 500 = 2,500 m.

items.q: How many grams are in 1 kilogram?
How many milliliters are in 1 liter?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth, so 1 L = 1,000 mL.

items.q: About what is the mass of a bag of sugar?
items.e: A bag of sugar is about 1 kilogram (1,000 g). 1 g is about the mass of a paper clip.

items.q: About how much does a teaspoon hold?
items.e: A teaspoon holds about 5 milliliters. 500 mL is about a big bottle of water.

items.q: About how much does a can of fizzy drink hold?
items.e: A can of drink holds about 330 milliliters, which is about one third of a liter.

items.q: Convert. 5 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so you need more grams: multiply. 5 × 1,000 = 5,000, so 5 kg = 5,000 g.

items.q: Convert. 6 L = ☐ mL
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. Liters are bigger than milliliters, so you need more milliliters: multiply. 6 × 1,000 = 6,000, so 6 L = 6,000 mL.

items.q: Convert. 3,000 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so you need fewer kilograms: divide. 3,000 ÷ 1,000 = 3, so 3,000 g = 3 kg.

items.q: Convert. 7,000 mL = ☐ l
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. Liters are bigger than milliliters, so you need fewer liters: divide. 7,000 ÷ 1,000 = 7, so 7,000 mL = 7 L.

items.q: Convert. 2 kg 300 g = ☐ g
Convert. 2 kg 30 g = ☐ g
items.e: 2 kg = 2,000 g. Add the 30 g: 2,000 + 30 = 2,030 g. Writing 230 g forgets that 2 kg is 2,000 g.

items.q: Convert. 1 L 750 mL = ☐ mL
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. Add the 750 mL: 1,000 + 750 = 1,750 mL. 850 mL would mean 1 L = 100 mL, which is wrong.

items.q: Which is the same as 3,450 g?
items.e: 1,000 g = 1 kg, so 3,000 g = 3 kg. 3,450 g = 3 kg and 450 g left over.

items.q: Which is the same as 4,080 mL?
items.e: 4,000 mL = 4 L. 4,080 mL = 4 L and 80 mL left over (not 800 mL: the 8 is in the tens place).
The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 4 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 200 ÷ 4 = 50 g. The needle is 1 mark past 600 g: 600 + 50 = 650 g.
Each kilogram is split into 5 equal spaces, so each mark is 1,000 ÷ 5 = 200 g. The needle is 2 marks past 2 kg: 2,000 + 400 = 2,400 g, which is 2 kg 400 g.
Each kilogram is split into 10 equal spaces, so each mark is 1,000 ÷ 10 = 100 g. The needle is 7 marks past 1 kg: 1,000 + 700 = 1,700 g, which is 1 kg 700 g.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mL. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 mL. The water is 1 line above 600 mL: 600 + 100 = 700 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mL. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 250 ÷ 5 = 50 mL. The water is 3 lines above 250 mL: 250 + 150 = 400 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug? Give your answer in liters and milliliters.
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 mL. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 500 ÷ 5 = 100 mL. The water is 3 lines above 1,000 mL: 1,000 + 300 = 1,300 mL. 1,000 mL = 1 L, so 1,300 mL = 1 L 300 mL.
